items.title: Australian arrested after teenage girl's body found in a suitcase in Thailand
items.description: An Australian man is in custody after the body of a teenage girl was found in a suitcase in Thailand.

items.title: These billionaires' kids are learning something most Australians are not
items.description: Rich and powerful families have a strong interest in one particular language, with experts saying it is no surprise given the country's rise.

items.title: Farewell: 27 things Virginia Trioli learned at the ABC
items.description: After almost 40 years in Australian journalism, 27 of them at the ABC, I am now in possession of enough mistakes to claim a small amount of experience.

items.title: Daughter of stabbing victims calls for better mobile coverage
items.description: The daughter of an elderly couple attacked in an alleged home invasion in northern NSW wants to see mobile coverage improved across regional areas.

items.title: Volunteers say hotline told them to collect dead bird against government advice
items.description: South Australian citizen scientists say they called the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline to report a dead sea bird and were given advice that contradicts official government messaging.

items.title: Australia's next opponent locked in after World Cup chaos
items.description: The Socceroos will meet Egypt in the knockout stage of the World Cup after a stunning finish in Group G. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Tempers flare between Power and Crows players in Showdown 60
items.description: Showdown 60 is a heated affair between the Power and Crows at Adelaide Ovall, while the Magpies enjoy their win over the Tigers, and the Blues make it six straight victories. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Left out Blue makes Origin statement as Sea Eagles dominate Storm
items.description: Manly enforcer Haumole Olakau'atu, who was left out of the NSW team in State of Origin Game II, has made a statement to Blues selectors with a dominating first half against the Melbourne Storm. Follow live.

items.title: In Beirut, a sacred ceremony also becomes display of Hezbollah's force
items.description: Tens of thousands of Shiite Muslims gathered in Beirut for the largest Ashura procession in years, as Hezbollah used the holy day to project strength despite growing pressure to disarm after months of war with Israel.

items.title: US strikes Iran after Trump calls Hormuz attack 'foolish' ceasefire breach
items.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards vows a "swift and decisive" response, according to Iranian state television, claiming they repelled a US attack on Sirik Island, on the shores of the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Why hasn't the global economy completely collapsed?
items.description: An unfortunate side effect of the incompetent and erratic negotiating tactics of the Trump administration is that some of the underlying stories in the global economy can get overlooked.

items.title: Heartbreaking scenes emerging from earthquakes in Venezuela
items.description: After two powerful earthquakes, rescue teams from around the globe are in a race against time to pull survivors from the rubble.

items.title: Live: Vixens and Fever meet for place in Super Netball grand final
items.description: Reigning champions Melbourne Vixens host Super Netball's preliminary final against the West Coast Fever, the team they defeated in last year's decider. Follow live.

items.title: Rescuers pin hopes on satellite tracker to help save entangled humpback whale
items.description: An entangled humpback whale near Sydney is one of eight currently caught in marine debris off the New South Wales coast.

items.title: A warm and comforting gnocchi bake
items.description: "This would be something I'd love to make on a Sunday and have it bubbling away while you're doing odd jobs around the house."

items.title: At 80, John Williamson is ready to hang up his guitar
items.description: Now that folk and country music legend John Williamson is 80, he wants to spend less time touring and more time at home eating his own tomatoes.

items.title: Photographer captures elders' stories and WA's stunning southern landscapes
items.description: A photography exhibition in Albany shares the stories of Menang elders, who often have been overlooked in history.

items.title: The dry heart of Australia is now awash with water
items.description: The myth of an inland sea lured 19th century European explorers into the heart of Australia. But where they found only desert, this year it's awash, with water levels at Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre now the best some locals have ever seen.

items.title: Crime scene declared after armed man shot by police south of Brisbane
items.description: An armed man has been shot by police south of Brisbane after he allegedly confronted officers while carrying a rifle.

items.title: While teaching about pancreatic cancer, John realised he ticked every box
items.description: Clinical worker John McNeur didn't realise he was unwell until he was delivering a health workshop on pancreatic cancer in the remote Northern Territory — and he began ticking all of the boxes. Now he's on a mission to raise awareness.

items.title: Shock results from peptide test reveal 'life-threatening' ingredients
items.description: Doctors warn of an "enormous" risk of overdose after testing of a popular unapproved weight loss peptide reveals the product had double the strength of what was listed on its label.

items.title: Described as a 'talented athlete', Hussein Dehaini was gunned down at 33
items.description: Those who knew Hussein Dehaini say he could have been anything he wanted to be. But his life ended at 33, when he was gunned down in the middle of a Melbourne street.

items.title: World Cup quick hits: Bedlam in Group H, Dua Lipa surprise and superstars warm the bench
items.description: Group H delivers us incredible drama, some of the World Cup's biggest stars find themselves warming the pine, and Dua Lipa makes a surprise appearance. Here are today's quick hits.

items.title: 'Systemic issue': Abuse sees Canberra referees quitting after a year
items.description: Canberra soccer match officials say referee abuse is a "systemic issue" across all sporting codes, with increasingly hostile behaviour from spectators, players and coaches causing 44 per cent of Capital Football's referees to leave their roles after a year.

items.title: 'God's gift to Indian cricket': The great expectations on teen wonder
items.description: On tour with India and on the brink of his international debut, the pressure is being heaped on 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.
